q: 1. For the manufacture of Portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are
explain: Portland cement raw materials are proportioned at roughly 63% lime, 22% silica, and 15% other ingredients.

q: 2. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts with water immediately and is the first compound to set.

q: 3. Soundness test of cement determines
explain: The soundness test checks for excess free lime or magnesia, which can cause delayed expansion and cracking.

q: 4. Quick lime is
explain: Quicklime is chemically calcium oxide (CaO), produced by burning (calcining) limestone.

q: 5. A mortar prepared by mixing wood powder or saw dust to the cement or lime mortar is known as
explain: Adding lightweight fillers like sawdust or wood powder to mortar produces light weight mortar.

q: 6. Which of the following is a rock Gypsum is rock as well as minerals?
explain: Gypsum is unique in being classified both as a mineral (a specific compound) and as a rock (gypsum rock, formed largely of that mineral).

q: 7. The purpose of adding pozzolana (surki) to lime is to
explain: Pozzolana reacts with lime to impart hydraulic properties, allowing the mortar to set and harden even under water.

q: 8. A sample of cement is said to be sound when it does not contain free
explain: A sound cement sample should be free of excess uncombined (free) lime, which causes delayed expansion.

q: 9. The small lumps of cement evolved after burning are named as
explain: Clinkers are the small, hard lumps produced when raw materials are burnt in the cement kiln, later ground into cement.

q: 10. Quick lime is a
options: product left immediately after the calcination of pure limestone
explain: Quicklime is the product remaining immediately after pure limestone is calcined, driving off carbon dioxide.

q: 11. which one is correct ?
options: quick lime generates heat on water addition
quick lime is obtained by calcination of pure lime
explain: All the statements are characteristics of quick lime (Calcium Oxide); it slakes rapidly, produces heat (exothermic), and is derived from calcining limestone.

q: 12. Lime having high calcium oxide content, which can set and become hard only in the presence of CO2 from the atmosphere is known as
explain: Fat lime (or rich lime) consists of high CaO content and hardens through carbonation, a process requiring CO2 from the air.

q: 13. While preparing lime mortar, the general ratio adopted in between lime and surkhi or sand is
explain: Lime mortar is commonly proportioned with lime to sand/surkhi in a ratio of about 1:2 to 1:3.

q: 14. A dry powder obtained on treating quick lime with just enough water... is called
explain: When just enough water is added to quicklime to complete the chemical reaction without making it a paste, it results in a dry powder called hydrated lime.

q: 15. Lime suitable for making mortar of good strength
explain: Hydraulic lime is the standard choice for load-bearing or high-strength mortar because of its superior binding properties.

q: 16. The process of heating the lime stone to redness in contact with air is termed
explain: Calcination is the thermal treatment of ores or minerals to effect a physical or chemical change, specifically the removal of CO2 from limestone.

q: 17. As per IS specification, the minimum time for initial setting of ordinary portland cement is
explain: IS codes specify that OPC must have an initial setting time of at least 30 minutes to allow for mixing and placement.

q: 18. A slow setting cement has higher percentage of
explain: Dicalcium Silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and contributes to long-term strength, whereas C3A causes fast setting.

q: 19. Dormant period (2-5hr) is concerned with
explain: The dormant period is a stage in the hydration process where the reaction rate slows down significantly, allowing for the placement and finishing of concrete.

q: 20. During production of cement raw materials are mixed in
explain: Ball mills use steel balls to grind and mix raw materials (dry or wet) into a fine powder or slurry.

q: 21. The amount of loss of ignition, insoluble residue & residual retained (OPC) on IS sieve
explain: Standard limits for OPC: Loss on Ignition (<4%), Insoluble Residue (<1.5%), and Sieve Residue (<10%).

q: 22. The strength of RHPC for one day is equal to... day of PPC
explain: Rapid Hardening Portland Cement (RHPC) is designed to achieve the 3-day strength of ordinary cement in just 1 day.

q: 23. The raw materials having more than 10% proportion in the manufacture of cement are
explain: Lime (CaO, 60-67%) and Silica (SiO2, 17-25%) are the two largest components of Portland cement.

q: 24. The temperature range at which the consistency test is conducted
explain: Vicat apparatus tests for consistency are standardized to be conducted in a room temperature range of 27 ± 2°C.

q: 25. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between
explain: Standard consistency is achieved when the Vicat plunger penetrates to a point 5-7mm from the bottom (33-35mm from top).

q: 26. In briquette test, the seven day tensile strength of good portland cement should not be less than
explain: Standard tensile strength for OPC at 7 days using the briquette method is typically around 2.5 MPa (25 kg/cm²).

q: 27. The dry process of manufacturing cement has become obsolete, because...
options: it is difficult to maintain correct proportions
explain: The key indicates 'all of the above', though modern industry actually prefers dry process for energy efficiency; historically, wet process offered better mixing.

q: 28. The quality of cement is good if it has more of
explain: High C3S content ensures better early strength and binding quality in Portland cement.

q: 29. Quick setting cement is used
options: where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick-setting cement is essential for underwater work where the cement must set before being washed away by currents.

q: 30. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of 5 minutes and a final setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 31. Compared to the ordinary portland cement, the ultimate strength of the pozzolona portland cement is
explain: While slow to start, PPC eventually achieves a higher ultimate strength due to the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrates.

q: 32. In low heat cement, the proportion of the following compound is kept at low value
explain: Both C3A and C3S produce significant heat; their levels are minimized in low-heat cement to prevent thermal cracking.

q: 33. During the test of portland cement for “loss of ignition” the loss in weight occurs due to
explain: High temperature drives off moisture and CO2 from carbonates present in the sample.

q: 34. If P is the percentage of water required for normal consistency, water to be added for determination of initial setting time is,
explain: For setting time tests, the water content is standardized at 0.85 times the water required for standard consistency.

q: 35. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plaster
explain: For internal plastering, a 1:4 mix (one part cement to four parts sand) is standard as it provides a good balance of workability and strength without excessive shrinkage.

q: 36. The rate of hydration and hydrolysis of cement depends upon its
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area exposed to water, increasing the rate of hydration and hydrolysis.

q: 37. The most commonly used retarder in cement is
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard the fast-setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate.

q: 38. The cement mortar mix generally used for ceiling plaster
explain: Ceiling plaster needs a richer mix (1:3) to provide better adhesion and to counteract the effects of gravity during application.

q: 39. The most commonly used retarder in cement is (Accelerator: CaCl2, Retarder: Gypsum)
explain: Gypsum is added during clinker grinding specifically to retard the fast setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate.

q: 40. The initial setting time of lime -pozzolana is
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures typically have a longer initial setting time of about 2 hours.

q: 41. An impermeable concrete is produced by
explain: Achieving impermeable concrete requires proper mixing, compaction, and curing together to minimize voids and ensure complete hydration.

q: 42. As the cement sets and hardens it generates heat. This is called
explain: The heat released during the chemical hydration reactions of cement is termed the heat of hydration.

q: 43. The seven days compressive strength of a good portland cement, as obtained form the compressive test of cement sand mortar should not be less than for tensile test: 20 and 25 kg/cm2 respectively.
explain: A good Portland cement should achieve a 7-day compressive strength of at least about 175 kg/cm2 in the standard mortar test.

q: 44. Concreting should be stopped when temperature falls below
explain: At low temperatures, the hydration process of cement slows down significantly; generally, precautions or stops are needed below 10°C (or 4.5°C depending on specific codes). The book key specifies 10°C.

q: 45. All burnt bricks should be soaked in water for at least ............ hours to be used with cement mortar.
explain: The key indicates 1/4 (0.25 hours or 15 minutes), though field practice often recommends longer, this value is extracted from the provided answer key.
